infrastructure: Kosovo has improving mobile and urban broadband connectivity, though infrastructure is significantly less developed than EU peers.
Pristina has basic digital infrastructure, with improvement supported by Western development aid.
Electricity reliability remains a constraint for data centre development.
talent: University of Pristina has limited computer science AI research capacity.
A young, growing population with increasing digital literacy.
Brain drain to EU countries (particularly Germany, Switzerland) is extensive.
governance: Kosovo is a young state with developing institutional capacity, pursuing EU accession.
Data protection aligned with GDPR through the Law on Personal Data Protection; the Information and Privacy Agency is the regulator.
Anti-corruption is a priority but progress is challenging.
investment: Limited AI-specific investment; economy relies on diaspora remittances and international development aid.
USAID and EU development funds support digital transformation.
economic_readiness: One of Europe's youngest and poorest economies, with limited domestic AI market.
Young population (average age ~30) with growing digital adoption.
Diaspora connections provide some international knowledge and capital access.
